login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to an existing account when the email matches.
saml.note: Cross-identity merges by matching verified email are documented behavior and should not be flagged as an identity-collision bug by themselves.

saml.description: Only verified email/phone values from social or enterprise SSO providers are synced into primaryEmail/primaryPhone.
saml.note: If an upstream unverified email/phone does not appear as the local primary identifier, that is expected behavior.

saml.description: API resource scopes or organization scopes not enabled for a third-party application are ignored and not granted.
saml.note: A missing permission in the resulting token may be due to app configuration, not enforcement at exchange time.

saml.description: Requesting a non-enabled user profile scope for a third-party application results in an authorization error.
saml.note: Scope-request failures can be expected configuration errors rather than authorization-binding vulnerabilities.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL.
saml.note: Expiry in this case reflects session binding by design, not necessarily refresh-token freshness enforcement.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests that expect JWT-decodable claims will misinterpret opaque tokens unless they use userinfo or introspection.

saml.description: Public clients may receive a new refresh token on every refresh when rotation is enabled.
saml.note: Refresh token value changes across exchanges are expected and should not be treated as session incoherence.

saml.constraint: SAML in the provided Logto docs is Logto-as-IdP only. There is no documented SAML Assertion Consumer Service endpoint where Logto consumes upstream SAMLResponse, so saml_login and create_provider for upstream SAML IdP testing are absent for this protocol run. Do NOT attempt SP-side forged-assertion tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience, replay tests) against Logto from these docs; they target a different product role.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the relevant setup surface is SAML application configuration, not upstream SAML login. Create a SAML application and configure ACS URL, SP Entity ID, NameID format, and optional assertion encryption through application settings; there is no documented API path for posting SAML assertions into Logto.

Applications using token exchange MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled in application settings. It is disabled by default; otherwise /oidc/token returns an error like 'token exchange is not allowed for this application'. This affects I5 token-exchange tests and any impersonation/PAT exchange setup.

Refresh token TTL has session-binding semantics: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After session expiry, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. For I2 freshness tests that rely on long-lived refresh tokens, include offline_access in the authorization request or results will reflect session expiry, not refresh-token policy.

Numeric sentinel/behavior: rotate_refresh_token defaults to true, and refresh token rotation behavior is conditional rather than per-use for confidential clients: a new refresh token is issued if one year has passed since rotation, or >=70% of original TTL has passed, or always for public clients. Do NOT assume every refresh request rotates for traditional web apps; for SPAs/native apps, do assume rotation on every refresh when enabled.

Numeric parameter meaning: refresh_token_ttl_days is unavailable for SPA clients, and TTL refreshment through token requests is unavailable in SPA for security reasons. Do NOT use SPA applications for refresh-token TTL extension tests; use traditional web or other non-SPA app types.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and audience-binding tests, request only scopes and resources that are enabled for the third-party application. Non-enabled user profile scopes cause an authorization error; non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. A missing claim in the exchanged token may therefore be by design due to app permission configuration, not a security control in token exchange.

For I5 organization permission tests, organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. If omitted, organization-related grants will not appear, causing false negatives in organization-bound authorization tests.

Redirect URI matching semantics are mixed: exact matching is standard, but wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, only in hostname/pathname, and wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For security-sensitive redirect/callback tests, prefer exact redirect URIs; wildcard behavior is by design and broadens accepted callbacks.

Usernames are case-sensitive by default, controlled by CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME. For I4 case-confusion tests involving username-based identities, treat 'Admin' and 'admin' as distinct by default. Changing this setting does not retroactively normalize existing data, so mixed historical data can produce ambiguous results unrelated to current auth logic.

Enterprise SSO account linking behavior is by design email-based: adding SSO links identities to existing accounts if the email matches; removing SSO removes linked SSO identities but retains the user account. For I4 saml_email_binding_collision-style reasoning, email-based merge/linking is expected behavior in Logto enterprise connectors and must not be flagged as a collision unless the merge exceeds documented email-linking intent.

For I3 signing-key rotation coherence tests on OSS, rotating signing keys requires a Logto instance restart before the new key takes effect. On Cloud, rotation takes effect immediately. Never rotate signing keys consecutively two or more times, as documented behavior may invalidate all issued tokens and confound coherence results.

Opaque vs JWT token format is request-dependent: if no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token intended for /oidc/me and introspection; when a specific resource or organization is requested, access tokens are JWTs by default. For verification and I2/I5 tests, choose the correct verifier: use /oidc/me or /oidc/token/introspection for opaque tokens, and do not expect JWT claims locally unless a resource/organization was requested.

SAML in Logto is IdP mode for SAML applications, not an upstream SAML broker login endpoint. Do NOT attempt to use a fabricated SAMLResponse/ACS-style saml_login attack sequence against Logto itself for this protocol run; the documented SAML flow is SP-initiated from your application to Logto, and Logto returns the SAML response to the external SP.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, use Management/API setup around SAML application creation and then test downstream OIDC/OAuth artifacts only where documented. There is no documented Logto endpoint here for creating an upstream SAML IdP connector or posting attacker-controlled SAMLResponse assertions, so saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_expired_assertion, saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience cannot be executed from the provided docs without inventing endpoints.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. For any I5 token-exchange test, update_application MUST enable token exchange first; otherwise failures like 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' are expected setup failures, not security rejections.

Refresh token/session binding sentinel: a refresh token issued without offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Do NOT assume refresh_token_ttl_days alone controls lifetime; include offline_access when testing long-lived refresh-token behavior.

Refresh token rotation behavior is conditional, not one-shot. When rotate_refresh_token is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh; other clients rotate when one year has passed or >=70% of original TTL has elapsed. Do NOT treat absence of immediate rotation on confidential clients as a replay flaw.

Numeric sentinel/default behavior: rotate_refresh_token defaults to true, refresh_token_ttl_days defaults to 14 for non-SPA apps, and TTL refreshment is unavailable in SPA. Do NOT assume omitted values mean zero or disabled behavior; omitted refresh-token settings inherit platform defaults.

Redirect URI matching for applications supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname, and only for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For I3/I5 tests involving redirect_uri changes, use exact or valid wildcard forms only; invalid wildcard placement causes setup failure, not a security decision.

User search parameter semantics: search fields default to fuzzy 'like' matching, with optional exact, similar_to, or posix modes. For I4 collision tests using verify_entity_details_by_name, exact-match scenarios MUST set mode or mode.<field>=exact; otherwise fuzzy matching can return unintended users and create false collision signals.

Case sensitivity in user search is controlled globally by isCaseSensitive and defaults to false. For I4 case_confusion tests, run both a case-sensitive and case-insensitive lookup strategy; otherwise merged search results may reflect search configuration rather than identity collapse.

Exact-match search parameters support exact string matching only; wildcards like '*' are not documented as glob semantics in exact mode. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, DO NOT set exact-match search values to '*' expecting wildcard behavior; omit the field restriction or use the documented fuzzy/regex modes instead.

Application ownership/tenant context is implicit in the current Logto tenant. The docs describe tenant-scoped resources and no create_tenant API in the provided material. Do NOT expect per-request owner fields for applications/users in these endpoints unless separately documented in OpenAPI.

SAML in the provided Logto docs is IdP mode only: Logto issues SAML assertions to external service providers. There is no documented SAML Assertion Consumer Service endpoint for Logto to consume upstream SAMLResponse assertions, so do NOT attempt upstream `saml_login` attack sequences against Logto for this protocol run; they are unsupported by these docs and would produce false positives.

For token-exchange tests, the target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled first. Token exchange is disabled by default; otherwise `/oidc/token` returns an error like 'token exchange is not allowed for this application'.

When testing refresh-token or long-lived session behavior, include `offline_access` in the authorization request if you need refresh tokens independent of the browser session. If a refresh token is issued without `offline_access`, it is session-bound and becomes invalid when the fixed 14-day session expires, regardless of the refresh token TTL setting.

Numeric sentinel semantics: `rotate_refresh_token` defaults to true, and `refresh_token_ttl_days` defaults to 14 for non-SPA apps. Do not treat omitted values as zero/disabled. SPA does not support TTL refreshment through token requests; rotation may still issue a new refresh token when necessary.

For public clients (SPA/native), when refresh-token rotation is enabled, a new refresh token will always be issued on refresh-token exchange. Tests that assume refresh token stability across exchanges will misinterpret by-design rotation as replay protection or session incoherence.

Do NOT use wildcard redirect URIs as a stand-in for permissive matching tests. Redirect URI wildcards are only supported for SPA and Traditional Web apps, only in hostname/pathname, and are explicitly non-standard OIDC with increased attack surface. They are unrelated to identity/principal matching semantics.

For I5 token-exchange audience/resource tests, always request a concrete `resource` or audience-bound token. Logto issues opaque access tokens when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request; opaque tokens are primarily for `/oidc/me` and general purposes, and cannot be used as organization tokens.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests on third-party/OIDC apps, only scopes enabled for that application are grantable. Non-enabled user profile scopes cause an authorization error; non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and will not appear on the consent screen or be granted. Distinguish 'ignored by policy' from 'broker over-granted'.

Organization permissions require `urn:logto:scope:organizations`. If that scope is not enabled/requested, organization scopes are ignored. For organization-bound I5 tests, include `urn:logto:scope:organizations` or the test will fail for setup reasons rather than authorization-binding reasons.

For I4 cross-user/case-confusion tests involving usernames, Logto username case sensitivity is deployment-configurable (`CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME`, default true). A case-folding collision is not a product bug unless the deployment has explicitly disabled case sensitivity. Record the deployment setting before interpreting `Admin` vs `admin` results.

Enterprise/SSO account linking behavior is email-based by design: adding SSO identities links to existing accounts if the email matches. Cross-protocol identity merges on matching email are therefore expected behavior, not an I4 violation, unless the merge occurs without the documented email match condition.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into `primaryEmail`, and only verified phone numbers are synced into `primaryPhone`. Tests that expect unverified upstream identifiers to bind local primary identifiers will produce false positives.

For I2 token freshness controls, include a valid control token alongside any attack token. Use a control with current-valid timing (for example, exp in the future and iat at now) so that a failed attack can be distinguished from broken client/app setup. This is especially important because Logto may issue opaque tokens depending on request shape.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
